title: Rahul Gandhi Detained and Released After Sit-In Outside PM Modi's Residence Over NEET Crisis
excerpt: The Congress leader, his sister Priyanka, and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav were forcibly removed by Delhi Police during a protest demanding the education minister's resignation.
body:
• Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday during a protest outside PM Modi's residence
  • Gandhi was seen lying on the road resisting police removal and reportedly suffered an injury below his eye during the scuffle
  • The sit-in demanded Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and a parliamentary discussion on the NEET exam paper leak
  • All leaders were released late Tuesday evening; the opposition vowed to raise the issue in Parliament's monsoon session

Delhi Police detained Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday after they staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence demanding accountability over the NEET-UG exam paper leak — a dramatic escalation that turned the ongoing student protest movement into a full-blown parliamentary confrontation.

Dramatic Scenes at Lok Kalyan Marg

Gandhi and several Congress leaders began a sit-in around 3:30 PM outside the gates of Lok Kalyan Marg, the official prime ministerial residence, demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and a parliamentary discussion on the NEET crisis.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=U9K8BZos11Q

When police moved to clear the protest, Gandhi was seen lying on the ground, resisting as security personnel attempted to lift him. An aide said he sustained an injury below his eye during the confrontation. Priyanka Gandhi was filmed clinging to the door of a police bus even after it began moving — a moment that quickly went viral on social media.

"An attack on students is an attack on every Indian family. PM Modi believes he can get away without answers, without consequences. He cannot. Not this time."

— Rahul Gandhi, before his detention

The Context

The opposition protest came a day after tens of thousands of students from the Cockroach Janta Party movement clashed with police during a march on Parliament, resulting in 180 injuries. The Congress party has been demanding Pradhan's resignation, action against those responsible for the exam leak that affected 2 million students, and a formal discussion in both houses of Parliament.

"Photo: Wikimedia Commons" style="max-width:100%;border-radius:8px" loading="lazy"><figcaption style="font-size:0.85rem;color:#666;margin-top:8px">Akhilesh Yadav."

https://www.instagram.com/p/DY9V89CgK0A/

Minister of State Jitendra Singh met Gandhi at the protest site and urged him to end the sit-in, offering to discuss the NEET issue in Parliament. Gandhi refused, insisting on Pradhan's resignation as a precondition.

Opposition Unity

The presence of SP chief Yadav alongside Gandhi was notable — signaling potential opposition coordination on an issue that cuts across party lines in northern India, where state elections loom in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh. Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan also joined the protest.

All detained leaders were released from Chhatrasal Stadium and Mandir Marg Police Station later Tuesday evening. Gandhi recorded a video from detention urging the prime minister to apologize to students.

The opposition has vowed to raise the NEET issue prominently during Parliament's monsoon session, setting up what could be weeks of legislative confrontation over India's education system and the government's handling of the student protest movement.
